Health Information Bill Second Reading debate

Second Reading12 January 2026 bill-773, bill-774, bill-775

A Second Reading debate on the Health Information Bill, which requires licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to the National Electronic Health Record and sets rules for access, sharing and safeguards.

The Bill requires all licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to NEHR, so a patient's records can follow them across providers. It allows patients to restrict access, while critical allergies and vaccination records remain visible, and prohibits access for employment or insurance purposes. The Minister says the Bill is intended to take effect from early 2027.

  • The Health Information Bill was moved for Second Reading.

    The Bill be now read a Second time.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • Singapore is ageing rapidly, with one in four Singaporeans aged 65 and above by 2030.

    By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • Currently, key health records are often not accessible across providers, which can risk medication errors, delayed treatment and duplicate tests.

    Such gaps can risk medication errors, delayed treatment and duplicate tests and procedures.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • The Bill requires all licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to NEHR.

    The HIB will require all healthcare providers licensed under the Healthcare Services Act 2020 and retail pharmacies licensed under the Health Products Act 2007 to contribute key health information about patients into NEHR.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • Key health information includes allergies, vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, laboratory test results, radiological images and discharge summaries.

    allergies, vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, laboratory test results, radiological images and discharge summaries
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • NEHR access for patient care is limited to licensed healthcare providers and their authorised individuals.

    NEHR access for patient care purposes will be limited to licensed healthcare providers and their authorised individuals.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • Accessing NEHR for employment or insurance purposes is strictly prohibited.

    Accessing NEHR for purposes relating to employment or insurance will be strictly prohibited.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • NEHR access is allowed for specified statutory medical examinations.

    NEHR access will therefore be allowed for these statutory medical examinations.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • Patients may restrict access to their NEHR information so that only select healthcare providers may have access.

    they may restrict access to their NEHR information so that only select healthcare providers may have this access.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • From the second half of this year, patients can place an Access Restriction through the HealthHub app.

    From the second half of this year, patients can do so through the HealthHub app.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • During medical emergencies, a patient's NEHR information may be accessed despite an Access Restriction, with only doctors allowed to 'break glass'.

    only doctors will be allowed to "break glass".

  • Non-NEHR health information may be shared without consent only if three key criteria are met.

    We will enable the scoped sharing of non-NEHR health information without an individual's consent only if three key criteria are met.

  • A first offence for unauthorised access of NEHR information under clause 38 carries a fine of up to $50,000, two years' imprisonment or both.

    a person convicted of an offence relating to unauthorised access of NEHR information under clause 38 faces a fine of up to $50,000, two years’ imprisonment or both, for a first offence.
    Mr Tan Kiat How

  • Healthcare providers that fail to put in place required cybersecurity or data security measures may face a fine of up to $1 million.

What happens next The Bill is intended to commence from early 2027, and MOH will announce further implementation details soon.

Open questions from this debate (10)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether the maximum fine of $1 million is sufficient to deter large healthcare organisations.
  • How MOH will ensure insurers cannot obtain NEHR-derived information through clinical notes or audit clauses.
  • What the exact funding quantum and eligibility criteria will be for small GP clinics.
  • Whether cybersecurity insurance will be offered to small providers.
  • How patients who are not digitally confident will be assisted to place or manage Access Restrictions.
  • When and whether community health partners beyond public entities will be added to the Fourth Schedule.
  • How overseas medical records will be treated in the NEHR.
  • What constitutes 'reasonable access' to NEHR for clinicians in practice.
  • How data breach notification thresholds will apply to smaller breaches.
  • Whether the list of statutory medical examinations will remain tightly scoped over time.
